th Order No.03/Dated- 11 April, 2025 I.A. No. 4142 of 2025 1.

This instant interlocutory application has been filed on behalf of appellant under Section 430(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of sentence dated 24.07.2024 passed by learned Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act, Palamau at Daltonganj, in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 09 of 2022, whereby and whereunder, the appellant has been convicted for the offences under Sections 354, 363 & 376(1) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 & 8 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and to pay fine of Rs. 20,000/- (Rs. Twenty Thousand) and in default of payment of the fine amount, to further undergo R.I. for four months for the offence punishable under Section 376(1) of the I.P.C.,
further sentenced to undergo R.I. for five years and to pay fine of Rs. 10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand)
and in default of payment of the fine amount, to further undergo R.I. for two months for the offence punishable under Section 363 of the I.P.C. and further sentenced to undergo R.I. for two years and to pay fine of Rs. 5,000/- (Rs. Five Thousand) and in default of payment of fine amount, to further undergo R.I. for one month for the offence punishable under Section 8 of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text:
It has been contended on behalf of the appellant that it is case where no case is made out for the penal offences under POCSO Act or even under Section 376 of the I.P.C.
3.

It has been contended that such submission has been made based upon the ground that if the testimony of the victim, who has been examined as P.W.-7, will be taken into consideration, it will be said to be consensual relationship which has been established by her with the present appellant with her own free will.

4. Further, the Doctor, who has been examined as P.W.-8, has mentioned in his report that he has found the single intra uterine embryo of 06 weeks and as such, it is evident therefrom that the victim was having physical relationship prior to the date of occurrence, as such, the instant case at best will be said to be consensual one and therefore, the ingredient of offences under POCSO Act will not be applicable herein.
5.
Learned counsel, based upon the aforesaid ground, has submitted that it is a fit case, where the sentence of the appellant is to be suspended.
6. While on the other hand, Mr. Shailesh Kumar Sinha, learned counsel appearing for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence.
7. It has been contended that since the conviction is also under POCSO Act as such, the consent is having no meaning.

The victim has fully supported the prosecution version and remained intact in the cross- examination and what she has deposed in the testimony, she has also stated in the statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
So far as the testimony of the Doctor is concerned that also clarifies that the appellant has committed physical assault / sexual assault with the victim.
8. Learned counsel for the State, based upon the aforesaid ground, has submitted that it is therefore not fit case for suspension of sentence.

9. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the finding recorded by the learned trial court in the impugned judgment as also the testimony of witnesses available in the trial court record and other material exhibits as available therein.

10. We, in order to appreciate the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties, has considered the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. wherein she has fully supported the prosecution version.
The aforesaid version has also been supported by the victim in her examination-in-chief as P.W.-7 and further, she remained consistent in her cross-examination.
The other witnesses have also supported the prosecution version.

Further, the age of the victim has been assessed to be less than 18 years based upon the Admit Card of Class-8, which has been marked 'Y'
for identification.
11. We have also considered the testimony of doctor, from which, it is evident that the victim was subjected to physical assault as consequence thereof, she was having the pregnancy of 06 weeks.

sentences.text: At this juncture, this Court is of the considered view that the meaning of consent so far as POCSO Act is concerned, is having no relevance.

The reasons for such view is that if the consent would have any relevance, then the question is that for what purpose the POCSO Act has been legislated when the penal provision as under Section 376 IPC was already there when the POCSO Act, 2012 has been notified.

13. It needs to refer herein that it is little more than a decade that the special Act (POCSO Act) is in operation and pertinent to note that at the time of introduction of the POCSO Act, "age of consent"
for unmarried girl was 16 and it was presumed that any one below this age cannot lawfully consent to sexual intercourse.

The POCSO Act raised the "age of consent" to 18 years and following the recommendations of Justice J.S. Verma Committee, in the wake of a gruesome incident, which took place in NCT, Section 375 of IPC was also amended by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013.

14. As a consequence of the aforesaid provisions, an act of sexual indulgence with a girl below 18 years, would attract the rigors of the POCSO Act as well as the offence under Section 376 of IPC, and it is being immaterial, whether it is a consensual relationship, as the law presume that a girl below 18 years is not capable of consenting to sexual intercourse and in such a scenario, even if a girl below 18, consent to a sexual intercourse, her consent must be ignored and the other party Shall be guilty of committing an offence under the POCSO Act.
15. The POCSO Act deals with number of situations in regard to sexual offence against children.
The relevant factor such as penetrated sexual assault as well as aggravated penetrated sexual assault depends on nature of sexual assault, therefore, the consent of minor, is immaterial.

16. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Satish Kumar Jayanti Lal Dabgar v. State of Gujarat,
(2015) 7 SCC 359 has categorically held that if the consent of minor is treated as a mitigating circumstance, it may lead to disastrous consequences.

entities.text:
Satish Kumar Jayanti Lal Dabgar v. State of Gujarat,
(2015) 7 SCC 359
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
For ready reference the relevant paragraph of the aforesaid judgment is being quoted as under:
"16.
Once we put the things in right perspective in the manner stated above, we have to treat it as a case where the appellant has committed rape of a minor girl which is regarded as a heinous crime.
Such an act of sexual assault has to be abhorred.
If the consent of minor is treated as a mitigating circumstance, it may lead to disastrous consequences.

This view of ours gets strengthened when we keep in mind the letter and 4 spirit behind the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012."
17.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Further, in the case of X Vs. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department,
Government of NCT of Delhi and Another"
(2023) 9 SCC 433 the Hon'ble Apex Court has laid down that in the matter of POCSO Act, consent has got no meaning.

----- The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ("the Pocso Act")
is gender neutral and criminalises sexual activity by those below the age of eighteen.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Under the Pocso Act, factual consent in a relationship between minors is immaterial.
18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent case of "X (Minor) Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Anr".

entities.text: X (Minor) Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 2373 has dealt with the issue of consent and has considered the averment in regard to love-affair and relevant paragraph No.6 is reproduced hereinafter :-
"6.
The High Court was manifestly in error in allowing the application for bail.

The reason that from the statement under Section 164 and the averments in the FIR, it appears that "there was a love affair" between the appellant and the second respondent and that the case was instituted on the refusal of the second respondent to marry the appellant, is specious.

Once, prima facie, it appears from the material before the Court that the appellant was barely thirteen years of age on the date when the alleged offence took place, both the grounds, namely that "there was a love affair"
between the appellant and the second respondent as well as the alleged refusal to marry, are circumstances which will have no bearing on the grant of bail.
Having regard to the age of the prosecutrix and the nature and gravity of the crime, no case for the grant of bail was established.

The order of the High Court granting bail has to be interfered with since the circumstances which prevailed with the High Court are extraneous in view of the age of the prosecutrix, having regard to the provisions of Section 376 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO."
19.
On the basis of discussion made hereinabove, this Court is of the view that since we are dealing with the case of minor, as such consent has got no meaning in the instant case.

20. The main limb of argument of appellant is that the appellant has established the sexual relationship with the consent of the victim, which according to considered view of this Court is not fit to be acceptable on the basis of the settled proposition of law as referred herein above,
21.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that it is not a fit case where the sentence of the appellant is to be suspended.
22. Accordingly, the instant interlocutory application being I.A. No. 4142 of 2025 stands dismissed.

23. It is made clear that any observation made hereinabove will not prejudice the case on merit,
since, the criminal appeal is pending before this Court for its consideration.
(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Sunil/
